claims.text: Formation and persistence of a protective oxide above 900 °C in CrFeCoNiX alloys is governed by selective oxidation of chromium and element X.
Al and Si have strong oxygen affinities that promote formation of a coherent protective oxide scale in CrFeCoNiAl and CrFeCoNiSi.
The protective scale consists of a Cr-rich oxide matrix containing embedded Al- or Si-oxide phases.
Embedded Al- or Si-oxides minimize oxide-growth stresses and accommodate misfit strain.
Protective-scale development proceeds through a diffusion-controlled oxidation mechanism.
Mn produces a less coherent oxide scale that is more prone to cracking and spallation than scales produced with Al or Si.
The investigated CrFeCoNiX alloys are single- or multiphase metallic solid solutions produced by conventional processing.
Element-specific oxidation behavior is controlled by the differing interactions of alloying elements with oxygen and by thermodynamic redox tendencies.
Selective oxidation of Cr and X determines oxide composition and growth kinetics.
Al- or Si-containing oxides densify the scale and improve adherence by lowering strain energy during growth.
Mn oxidation yields either greater volumetric expansion or less coherent oxide grain boundaries.
Greater volumetric expansion or less coherent grain boundaries in Mn-containing scales facilitate cracking and spallation.
CrFeCoNiAl and CrFeCoNiSi will develop thinner, more uniform, and more adherent oxide scales than CrFeCoNiMn and CrFeCoNi.
Al- and Si-containing alloys will exhibit slower oxide growth, lower weight gain, and fewer cracks or spallation defects during prolonged exposure.
CrFeCoNi without X is expected to form a less coherent, faster-growing, crack-prone scale.
The proposed comparison applies above 900 °C in oxidative or corrosive atmospheres for exposures of approximately 100 hours or longer.
Processing-derived microstructural heterogeneity may affect oxide-scale behavior.
